house_checks: • Zoning district RS-1-7 (San Diego Municipal Code, Chapter 13 (Zones)) — The purpose of the RS zones is to provide appropriate regulations for the development of single dwelling units that accommodate a variety of lot sizes and residential dwelling types and which promote neighborhood quality, character, and livability. (SDMC §131.0403(a)). RS-1-7 allows 1 dwelling unit per lot (SDMC §131.0431, Table 131-04D). Minimum lot: 5,000 sq ft, 50 ft wide (55 ft on a corner), 50 ft of street frontage and 95 ft deep (SDMC §131.0431, Table 131-04D); this lot (about 4,537 sq ft by its parcel outline) is smaller. Minimum setbacks: front 15 ft, side 4 ft, street side 5 ft, rear 13 ft (SDMC §131.0431, Table 131-04D; note 2: See Section 131.0443(a)(4).); the table's footnotes and SDMC §131.0443 adjust these in some cases, which aren't checked here. Height: listed as 24/30 ft (SDMC §131.0431, Table 131-04D), so no part above 30 ft, and "Maximum structure height shall not exceed the height of the angled building envelope plane, which connects the maximum structure height adjacent to the setback and the overall maximum structure height as determined by the underlying base zone and the requirements below." (SDMC §131.0444(a), (c)). Planned districts, overlay zones (such as the Coastal Overlay Zone) and state law (ADUs, SB 9) can change these; overlay zones and planned districts aren't checked here.

? Floor area allowed by zoning — Up to about 2,722 sq ft of gross floor area on this ~4,537 sq ft lot (FAR 0.60, SDMC §131.0446(a)(1), Table 131-04J, row "4.001 - 5,000 | 0.60"). On a lot over the minimum area that is mostly steep hillside the ratio is figured differently (SDMC §131.0446(a)(2)); slope isn't checked here. The Assessor records 1,733 sq ft of living area, so about 989 sq ft remain by this measure; the Assessor's living area isn't gross floor area and is incomplete, so this is a screening figure.

✗ Second home (two-family or more) — RS-1-7 allows 1 dwelling unit per lot under the base zone (SDMC §131.0431, Table 131-04D). State law can allow more (an ADU, a junior ADU, or an SB 9 two-unit project); those are the rows below.
✗ Split into two lots (by area only) — Two lots would each need at least 5,000 sq ft under RS-1-7 (SDMC §131.0431); this lot has about 4,537 sq ft. A state-law (SB 9) split has its own rules.
• Detached ADU (backyard home) — Building footprint is not on file, so open yard space cannot be verified without a site plan or survey.

? Second story — One story (inferred (assumption: single-story layout)). The height limit here is 30 ft (SDMC §131.0431); the floor area allowed is above. Foundation inspection required to carry upper-floor loads.
? Rooftop deck — Requires a flat roof or flat garage roof section.
